case.summary: Verdict is fraud at probability 0.77 for transaction 3503878 ($99.92, online, product R), a single-transaction card_not_present_new_device episode on a brand-new strong device profile (Windows | other | chrome 61.0 | 1280x720, first use ever on this card); exposure is $99.92. The decisive evidence is the memory family: a calibrated score of cms_p 0.849/cal_p 0.7674 and three prior confirmed-fraud closed cases on this exact card in the last four months (CC-2011, CC-2860, CC-5026), against a countervailing history-family reading that the amount sits inside the card's normal baseline and one prior same-template alert cleared after customer confirmation (CC-2087) — a genuine conflict between one strong fraud family and one legitimacy family. We asked for step-up authentication on the online purchase per §3b/§5 rather than blocking outright at 0.70≤p<0.85 with a single fraud family; the reply is assumed inconclusive/no response within the window, so per R4 the case adds MONITOR_CARD and DECLINE_TRANSACTION for the pending authorization while the CREATE_CASE and fraud-band BLOCK_CARD stand, all routed to L1 (exposure ≤$2,500) except the auto-routed CREATE_CASE/MONITOR_CARD; no SAR is filed since exposure is under $1,000 and device_neighbors found no fraud-linked ring on this profile (only 3 cards, 0 fraud cases). An alternative reading is that this is simply a legitimate new-device purchase, consistent with the earlier cleared travel/new-phone precedent CC-2087 and an in-baseline amount, but the card's repeated recent confirmed-fraud history keeps it in the fraud band pending a completed verification.
